function.name: alloc_user_handle
function.description: This function allocates a user handle, sets its type, and associates it with a pointer. If the handle is successfully allocated, it is stored in the client_objects array at the index derived from the handle.

parameters.name: ptr
parameters.description: This is the pointer that will be associated with the allocated user handle.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: This is the type that will be set for the allocated user handle.

function.return_type: HANDLE, which represents the allocated user handle. If the handle allocation fails, it returns 0.

function.name: is_valid_entry_uniq
function.description: This function checks if a given entry is valid and unique based on the provided handle, type, and unique identifier.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: This is used to identify a particular object or instance.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: This represents the type of the entry.

parameters.name: uniq
parameters.description: This is a unique identifier for the entry.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the entry is valid and unique or not.

function.name: is_valid_entry
function.description: This function checks if a user entry is valid based on the provided handle and type.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: This is a handle to the user entry that needs to be validated.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: This is the type of the user entry that needs to be validated.

function.return_type: BOOL, where TRUE indicates that the user entry is valid and FALSE indicates that it is not.

function.name: read_acquire_user_entry
function.description: This function reads and acquires a user entry from a source and copies it to a destination. It also checks the validity of the entry's unique identifier.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Handle to the user entry

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of the user entry

parameters.name: src
parameters.description: Source from where the user entry is to be read and acquired

parameters.name: dst
parameters.description: Destination where the user entry is to be copied

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the unique identifier of the destination matches the source, otherwise returns FALSE

function.name: get_user_entry
function.description: This function retrieves a user entry from a shared session based on the provided handle and type. It also sets the full handle based on the index and generation of the user entry.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Handle to the user entry to be retrieved

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of the user entry to be retrieved

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: Pointer to a user_entry struct where the retrieved entry will be stored

parameters.name: full
parameters.description: Pointer to a HANDLE where the full handle will be stored

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the user entry was successfully retrieved and FALSE otherwise

function.name: get_user_entry_at
function.description: This function retrieves a user entry at a specified index, checks the validity of the index, reads the user entry, and assigns a handle to the 'full' parameter.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The index at which the user entry is to be retrieved

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type of the user entry

parameters.name: entry
parameters.description: A pointer to the user entry structure where the retrieved entry will be stored

parameters.name: full
parameters.description: A pointer to a HANDLE where the handle from the index and generation of the entry will be stored

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the user entry is successfully retrieved and FALSE otherwise

function.name: get_shared_window
function.description: This function retrieves a shared window object. If the lock id is not set, it finds the shared session object. If the object is not found or the lock id is set but the shared object release sequence lock fails, it acquires a sequence lock on the shared object and sets the window shared memory pointer to the window shared memory of the object and the lock id to the object id. If the user entry cannot be retrieved, it returns an invalid handle status. If all operations are successful, it returns a success status.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Handle to the user object

parameters.name: lock
parameters.description: Pointer to the object lock structure

parameters.name: window_shm
parameters.description: Pointer to the pointer of the window shared memory structure

function.return_type: NTSTATUS, represents the status of the operation. It can be STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE if the user entry cannot be retrieved or the shared session object is not found, STATUS_PENDING if the sequence lock is acquired, or STATUS_SUCCESS if all operations are successful.

function.name: get_window_class_locator
function.description: This function retrieves the class locator of a window by its handle. It initializes an object lock, gets the shared window, and assigns the class locator to the locator variable. If the status is not successful, it resets the locator.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window for which the class locator is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: struct obj_locator, which represents the class locator of the window.

function.name: get_user_handle_ptr
function.description: This function retrieves a pointer to a user handle. It checks if the handle is valid and if it belongs to the current process. If the handle is invalid or belongs to another process, it returns NULL or a pointer to an object in another process respectively.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The handle to the user object.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type of the user object.

function.return_type: void pointer. It represents a pointer to the user object if the handle is valid and belongs to the current process, NULL if the handle is invalid, or a pointer to an object in another process if the handle belongs to another process.

function.name: next_thread_user_object
function.description: This function iterates over user entries starting from a given index. It checks each entry for a specific type and whether it belongs to the current process and thread. If such an entry is found, it returns the corresponding client object. If no such entry is found, it returns NULL.

parameters.name: tid
parameters.description: Thread identifier to match in the user entries.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Pointer to a handle. The function starts searching from the user entry corresponding to this handle.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of user entry to match.

function.return_type: void*: Returns a pointer to the client object corresponding to the first matching user entry. If no matching entry is found, it returns NULL.

function.name: set_user_handle_ptr
function.description: This function sets a user handle pointer to a specified value.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: This is the user handle that needs to be set.

parameters.name: ptr
parameters.description: This is the pointer value to which the user handle needs to be set.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value.

function.name: release_user_handle_ptr
function.description: This function releases a user handle pointer after making sure it is not null and not pointing to another process object. It also unlocks the user.

parameters.name: ptr
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the user handle that needs to be released.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: free_user_handle
function.description: This function is used to free a user handle. It first gets the user handle pointer. If the pointer is valid and not pointing to another process, it starts a server request to free the user handle. If the server call is successful, it sets the client object at the index derived from the handle to NULL.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: This is the user handle that needs to be freed.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: This represents the type of the user handle.

function.return_type: void pointer. It represents the pointer to the user handle. If the server call to free the handle is successful, it returns NULL, otherwise, it returns the original pointer.

function.name: detach_client_surfaces
function.description: This function detaches client surfaces from a given window handle, locks the surfaces for thread safety, removes the surfaces from the client_surfaces list and adds them to a detached list, then releases the surfaces.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window from which the client surfaces are to be detached.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: update_client_surfaces
function.description: This function updates the client surfaces associated with a given window handle. It locks the surfaces list, iterates over it, and if the surface's window handle matches the provided one, it updates the surface and sets its 'updated' flag to 1. After the update, it unlocks the surfaces list.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window whose associated client surfaces need to be updated.

function.return_type: void, meaning this function does not return anything

function.name: client_surface_create
function.description: This function creates a new client surface, initializes it, and adds it to the client surfaces list.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The size of the client surface to be created

parameters.name: funcs
parameters.description: Pointer to the client surface functions

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window where the client surface is to be created

function.return_type: void *: Returns a pointer to the created client surface. Returns NULL if the surface could not be created.

function.name: client_surface_add_ref
function.description: This function increments the reference count of a client surface.

parameters.name: surface
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the client surface whose reference count is to be incremented.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value.

function.name: client_surface_release
function.description: This function decreases the reference count of the client surface. If the reference count reaches zero, it locks the surfaces, detaches the surface if it has a window handle, removes the surface from the list, unlocks the surfaces, destroys the surface and finally frees the memory allocated to the surface.

parameters.name: surface
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to the client surface that needs to be released.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: client_surface_present
function.description: This function locks the surfaces, checks if the surface has a window handle, and if it does, it gets the device context if the surface is offscreen. It then calls the present function of the surface with the surface and device context as parameters. If a device context was obtained, it releases it. Finally, it unlocks the surfaces.

parameters.name: surface
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the client surface structure that is to be presented.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

function.name: is_client_surface_window
function.description: This function checks if the given window handle (HWND) matches the window handle stored in the client_surface structure. It returns TRUE if they match, FALSE otherwise. It also handles thread safety with the use of pthread_mutex_lock and pthread_mutex_unlock.

parameters.name: surface
parameters.description: Pointer to the client_surface structure which contains the window handle to be compared.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: The window handle to be compared with the one stored in the client_surface structure.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the window handle provided matches the one in the client_surface structure or not.

function.name: get_hwnd_message_parent
function.description: This function retrieves the parent window of the current message. If the message window does not exist, it triggers the creation of the desktop window. It then returns the handle to the message window.
function.return_type: HWND, which represents a handle to the parent window of the current message

function.name: get_full_window_handle
function.description: This function retrieves the full window handle for a given window handle. It performs various checks and transformations on the input handle, and may return the input handle itself or a handle obtained from the get_user_entry function.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is the handle to the window for which the full handle is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: HWND, which represents the full window handle for the given window handle.

function.name: is_desktop_window
function.description: This function checks if the provided window handle corresponds to the top window or the message window of the current thread.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window that needs to be checked.

function.return_type: BOOL, where TRUE indicates that the provided window handle corresponds to either the top window or the message window of the current thread, and FALSE otherwise.

function.name: get_win_ptr
function.description: This function retrieves a pointer to a window object based on the provided window handle. If the window belongs to another process, it checks if it's a desktop window and adjusts the pointer accordingly.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window for which the pointer is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: WND pointer, which represents the pointer to the window object.

function.name: is_current_thread_window
function.description: This function checks if the current thread is associated with the given window handle.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window to be checked.

function.return_type: HWND, represents the handle to the window if the current thread is associated with the window, otherwise returns 0.

function.name: is_current_process_window
function.description: This function checks if the given window handle belongs to the current process.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window that needs to be checked.

function.return_type: HWND, which is a handle to the window if it belongs to the current process, otherwise it returns 0.

function.name: is_window
function.description: This function checks if the provided window handle is valid.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is the handle to the window that needs to be checked.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window handle is valid, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: get_window_thread
function.description: This function retrieves the thread identifier and process identifier for the window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window.

parameters.name: process
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable that receives the process identifier. If this parameter is not NULL, get_window_thread copies the identifier of the process to the variable; otherwise, it does not.

function.return_type: DWORD, represents the identifier of the thread that created the window. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

function.name: get_parent
function.description: This function retrieves the parent window of the given window handle. If the window is a top-level window, the function retrieves the owner of the window. If the window is a child window, the function searches for the parent window. The function also handles error conditions and returns 0 if the window handle is invalid or if the window is a desktop window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window whose parent or owner is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: HWND. This is a handle to the parent or owner window. If the window does not have a parent or owner, or if the function fails, the return value is 0.

function.name: NtUserSetParent
function.description: This function sets a new parent for a given window. It also handles various error conditions, such as invalid parameters or window handles, and adjusts the window's position and visibility accordingly.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose parent is to be changed.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Handle to the new parent window.

function.return_type: HWND. Returns the handle to the old parent window if the function succeeds. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

function.name: get_window_relative
function.description: This function retrieves a handle to a window that has the specified relationship (Z-Order or owner) to the specified window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to a window. The window handle retrieved is relative to this window, based on the value of the rel parameter.

parameters.name: rel
parameters.description: The relationship between the specified window and the window whose handle is to be retrieved. This parameter can be one of the following values: GW_HWNDFIRST, GW_HWNDLAST, GW_HWNDNEXT, GW_HWNDPREV, GW_OWNER, GW_CHILD.

function.return_type: HWND. If the function succeeds, the return value is a window handle. If no window exists with the specified relationship to the specified window, the return value is NULL. To get extended error information, call GetLastError.

function.name: list_window_parents
function.description: This function lists the parents of a given window. It first tries to do this locally, but if a parent belongs to another process, it queries the server. The function dynamically allocates and grows a list to store the parent windows.
function.return_type: HWND pointer. It represents a pointer to a list of parent windows. If the function fails, it returns NULL.

function.name: list_window_children
function.description: This function lists all the child windows of a given window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the parent window.

function.return_type: Returns a pointer to an array of HWNDs representing the child windows. If the function fails, it returns NULL.

function.name: NtUserGetAncestor
function.description: This function retrieves the ancestor of the specified window based on the specified type.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window whose ancestor is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The ancestor type. This parameter can be one of the following values: GA_PARENT, GA_ROOT, GA_ROOTOWNER.

function.return_type: HWND. It represents the handle to the ancestor window if the function succeeds. Otherwise, it returns NULL.

function.name: is_child
function.description: This function checks if a given window (child) is a child of another window (parent). It retrieves the style of the child window and checks if it has the WS_CHILD style. It then gets a list of the child window's parents and checks if any of them are the parent window. If it finds a match, it checks if the parent window and the next window in the list are not NULL, and if so, sets the return value to TRUE. If it doesn't find a match or if a window in the list does not have the WS_CHILD style, it breaks the loop and returns the result.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Handle to the parent window.

parameters.name: child
parameters.description: Handle to the child window.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window is a child of the parent window, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: is_window_visible
function.description: This function checks if a window is visible by examining its style and its parent windows' styles.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window to be checked.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window is visible, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: is_window_drawable
function.description: This function checks if a window is drawable based on its style, visibility, minimization status, and icon. It also checks if the window's parents are visible and not minimized.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window to check.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: A boolean value that indicates whether the window has an icon.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window is drawable, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: is_window_unicode
function.description: This function checks if a window is Unicode or not.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window to be checked.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window is Unicode, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: NtUserEnableWindow
function.description: This function enables or disables a window based on the 'enable' parameter. If the window is being enabled, it sets the window style bits, sends a message to the window, and notifies the window event. If the window is being disabled, it sends a cancel mode message to the window, sets the window style bits, checks if the window is in focus and if so, removes the focus, and sends a message to the window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window to be enabled or disabled.

parameters.name: enable
parameters.description: Boolean value that determines whether to enable or disable the window. TRUE to enable the window, FALSE to disable it.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the operation was successful or not. Returns FALSE if the operation fails, otherwise returns TRUE.

function.name: is_hung_app_window
function.description: This function checks if a given application window is not responding.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window to be checked.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window is not responding, otherwise FALSE.

function.name: is_window_enabled
function.description: This function checks if a window is enabled by getting the window style and checking if the WS_DISABLED bit is not set.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window to check.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window is enabled, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: get_window_dpi_awareness_context
function.description: This function retrieves the DPI awareness context of a specified window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window whose DPI awareness context is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: UINT, represents the DPI awareness context of the window. If the function fails, it returns 0.

function.name: get_dpi_for_window
function.description: This function retrieves the DPI (dots per inch) for a specific window. It first gets the DPI awareness context for the window. If the context is monitor aware, it retrieves the DPI from the window's monitor. Otherwise, it gets the DPI from the context.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window for which the DPI is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: UINT, which represents the DPI for the specified window.

function.name: get_last_active_popup
function.description: This function retrieves the last active popup window associated with the specified window handle.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window.

function.return_type: HWND, which represents the handle to the last active popup window.

function.name: get_win_data
function.description: This function retrieves data from a given memory location and returns it as a LONG_PTR. The type of data retrieved depends on the size parameter, it can be a WORD, DWORD or LONG_PTR.

parameters.name: ptr
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the memory location from where the data is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: This parameter determines the type of data to be retrieved. It should be the size of either a WORD, DWORD or LONG_PTR.

function.return_type: LONG_PTR, which represents the data retrieved from the memory location pointed to by ptr.

function.name: set_win_data
function.description: This function sets the value of a given pointer based on the size provided. It uses memcpy to copy the value into the pointer. The size determines the type of the value to be copied.

parameters.name: ptr
parameters.description: This is the pointer to which the value will be copied.

parameters.name: val
parameters.description: This is the value that will be copied to the pointer.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: This determines the type of the value to be copied. It can be the size of a WORD or DWORD, or any other size.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return any value.

function.name: is_iconic
function.description: This function checks if a window is minimized (iconic).

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This parameter is a handle to the window.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window is minimized, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: is_zoomed
function.description: This function checks if a window is maximized or not.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This parameter is a handle to the window.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns true if the window is maximized, false otherwise.

function.name: get_window_long_size
function.description: This function retrieves information about a window, given its handle, offset, size, and ANSI flag. The information retrieved depends on the offset value provided.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window for which information is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Specifies the zero-based offset to the value to be retrieved.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Specifies the size of the value to be retrieved.

parameters.name: ansi
parameters.description: A flag that indicates whether the function should retrieve ANSI or Unicode window information.

function.return_type: LONG_PTR, represents the requested value if the function succeeds. Otherwise, it returns zero.

function.name: get_window_long
function.description: This function retrieves information about the specified window. The function also retrieves the 32-bit (long) value at the specified offset into the extra window memory.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window and context for the function

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The zero-based offset to the value to be retrieved. Valid values are in the range zero through the number of bytes of extra window memory, minus four; for example, if you specified 12 or more bytes of extra memory, a value of 8 would be an index to the third 32-bit integer.

function.return_type: DWORD, represents the 32-bit value at the specified offset.

function.name: get_window_long_ptr
function.description: This function retrieves information about the specified window. The function also retrieves the 32-bit (long) value at the specified offset into the extra window memory.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window and, indirectly, the class to which the window belongs.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The zero-based offset to the value to be retrieved. Valid values are in the range zero through the number of bytes of extra window memory, minus four; for example, if you specified 12 or more bytes of extra memory, a value of 8 would be an index to the third 32-bit integer.

parameters.name: ansi
parameters.description: A flag indicating whether the function should operate in ANSI or Unicode mode. If this parameter is TRUE, the function operates in ANSI mode.

function.return_type: ULONG_PTR and it represents the requested 32-bit value from the specified window's extra memory.

function.name: get_window_word
function.description: This function retrieves the word at the specified offset in the extra window memory of the given window. If the offset is invalid, it sets the last error to ERROR_INVALID_INDEX and returns 0.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose extra window memory is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Specifies the zero-based offset to the value to be retrieved. Valid values are in the range zero through the number of bytes of extra window memory, minus the size of a WORD.

function.return_type: WORD. It represents the word at the specified offset in the extra window memory. If the offset is invalid, the function returns 0.

function.name: set_window_style_bits
function.description: This function modifies the style of a window by setting and clearing specific style bits. It also handles visibility changes and updates the window state if necessary.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window whose style is to be modified.

parameters.name: set_bits
parameters.description: The style bits to be set (turned on) for the window.

parameters.name: clear_bits
parameters.description: The style bits to be cleared (turned off) for the window.

function.return_type: UINT, represents the old style of the window before the modification. If the function fails, it returns 0.

function.name: NtUserAlterWindowStyle
function.description: This function alters the style of a window based on the provided mask and style parameters.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose style is to be altered.

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: An unsigned integer representing the mask for the window style.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: An unsigned integer representing the new style for the window.

function.return_type: ULONG, represents the result of setting the window style bits. Returns non-zero if the operation was successful, zero otherwise.

function.name: fix_exstyle
function.description: This function modifies the extended style of a window based on its current style and extended style.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: The current style of the window.

parameters.name: exstyle
parameters.description: The current extended style of the window.

function.return_type: DWORD representing the modified extended style of the window.

function.name: set_window_owner
function.description: This function sets the owner of a window. It first checks if the window exists and is not a desktop or another process window. If it is valid, it sends a request to the server to set the window owner. After the server call, it releases the window pointer and returns the previous owner of the window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose owner is to be set.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Handle to the window that is to be set as the owner.

function.return_type: HWND, represents the handle to the previous owner of the window. If the window is invalid, desktop, or belongs to another process, it returns 0.

function.name: set_window_long
function.description: This function is used to change an attribute of the specified window. The function also sets a value at the specified offset in the extra window memory.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window and, indirectly, the class to which the window belongs.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Specifies the zero-based offset to the value to be set. Valid values are in the range zero through the number of bytes of extra window memory, minus the size of an integer.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Specifies the size of the parameter to be set.

parameters.name: newval
parameters.description: Specifies the replacement value.

parameters.name: ansi
parameters.description: Specifies whether the window is ANSI or not.

function.return_type: LONG_PTR. If the function succeeds, the return value is the previous value of the specified offset. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

function.name: NtUserSetWindowWord
function.description: This function sets a new value to a window word if the offset is valid. If the offset is less than 0 and not equal to GWLP_USERDATA, it sets the last Win32 error to ERROR_INVALID_INDEX and returns 0. Otherwise, it sets the window long with the new value.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The zero-based byte offset into the extra window memory

parameters.name: newval
parameters.description: The replacement value

function.return_type: WORD, represents the previous value of the specified 16-bit integer if the function succeeds. If the function fails, the return value is zero

function.name: NtUserSetWindowLong
function.description: This function sets the value of a specified offset in the extra window memory.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window and context for the function

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Specifies the zero-based offset to the value to be set

parameters.name: newval
parameters.description: Specifies the replacement value

parameters.name: ansi
parameters.description: Specifies whether the system should treat the value as ANSI or Unicode

function.return_type: LONG, represents the previous value of the specified offset in the extra window memory

function.name: NtUserSetWindowLongPtr
function.description: This function sets the value of a specified offset in the extra window memory.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window and specifies the window whose window memory will be set.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Specifies the zero-based byte offset in the window memory.

parameters.name: newval
parameters.description: Specifies the replacement value.

parameters.name: ansi

function.name: set_window_pixel_format
function.description: This function sets the pixel format of a window. If the window is not valid or is a desktop or other process window, it returns false. If the 'internal' parameter is true, it sets the internal pixel format to the specified format. Otherwise, it sets the internal pixel format to 0 and the pixel format to the specified format. After setting the pixel format, it releases the window pointer and updates the window state.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the pixel format is to be set.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: The pixel format to be set.

parameters.name: internal
parameters.description: Determines whether the internal pixel format is to be set (if true) or the pixel format (if false).

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the pixel format was successfully set. Returns TRUE if successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: get_window_pixel_format
function.description: This function retrieves the pixel format of a window. If the window is not valid or is a desktop or other process window, it returns 0. Otherwise, it returns the internal pixel format if it exists and the internal parameter is true, or the window's pixel format.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window for which the pixel format is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: internal
parameters.description: This parameter determines whether to return the internal pixel format (if it exists) or the window's pixel format.

function.return_type: int, representing the pixel format of the window. If the window is not valid or is a desktop or other process window, it returns 0. Otherwise, it returns the internal pixel format if it exists and the internal parameter is true, or the window's pixel format.

function.name: window_has_client_surface
function.description: This function checks if a window has a client surface by comparing the window handle with the handles of all client surfaces. It also checks if the window has a pixel format or internal pixel format.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window for which the function checks if it has a client surface.

function.return_type: int, where the return value is TRUE if the window has a client surface or a pixel format or internal pixel format, and FALSE otherwise.

function.name: NtUserGetProp
function.description: This function retrieves a property from a window object.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window for which the property is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: str
parameters.description: A pointer to the string that represents the property name.

function.return_type: HANDLE, represents the handle to the property if the function succeeds. Otherwise, it returns NULL.

function.name: NtUserSetProp
function.description: This function is used to set a property for a window. It communicates with a server to set the window property.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window for which the property is to be set.

parameters.name: str
parameters.description: A pointer to a string that specifies the property name.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: A handle to the property data.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was successful in setting the property or not.

function.name: NtUserRemoveProp
function.description: This function removes a property from a window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window from which the property will be removed.

parameters.name: str
parameters.description: A pointer to a string that specifies the string of the property to be removed.

function.return_type: HANDLE, represents a handle to the property that was removed. If the property was not previously set, the return value is NULL.

function.name: NtUserBuildPropList
function.description: This function builds a list of properties for a given window handle.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which to build the property list.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of properties to retrieve.

parameters.name: buffer
parameters.description: Pointer to the buffer that receives the property list.

parameters.name: ret_count
parameters.description: Pointer to a variable that receives the number of properties written to the buffer.

function.return_type: NTSTATUS, represents the completion status of the function. It can return STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER if the buffer or ret_count is NULL, STATUS_NO_MEMORY if memory allocation fails, or STATUS_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL if the buffer size is insufficient.

function.name: mirror_rect
function.description: This function mirrors a rectangle along the y-axis within another rectangle.

parameters.name: window_rect
parameters.description: This is the rectangle within which the other rectangle is mirrored.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: This is the rectangle that is mirrored within the window_rect.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: get_window_rects
function.description: This function retrieves the window rectangles (window, client, visible) for a given window handle and coordinate type. It also adjusts the rectangles based on the DPI settings.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the rectangles are to be retrieved.

parameters.name: relative
parameters.description: Specifies the type of coordinates to be used for the rectangles.

parameters.name: rects
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure that receives the window rectangles.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: Specifies the DPI settings to be used for adjusting the rectangles.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully retrieves the window rectangles, otherwise FALSE.

function.name: get_window_rect_rel
function.description: This function retrieves the coordinates of a window relative to the screen or client area, depending on the specified relative coordinate system.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose coordinates are to be retrieved.

parameters.name: rel
parameters.description: Specifies the coordinate system to be used.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that receives the screen or client coordinates of the window.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: Specifies the dots per inch (dpi) for the window.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function succeeds, or FALSE otherwise.

function.name: get_window_rect
function.description: This function retrieves the dimensions of the bounding rectangle of the specified window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that receives the screen coordinates of the upper-left and lower-right corners of the window.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI for the window.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was successful in retrieving the window rectangle or not.

function.name: get_client_rect_rel
function.description: This function gets the client rectangle relative to the window rectangle.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window.

parameters.name: rel
parameters.description: Specifies the coordinates relative to which the function should retrieve the rectangle.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that receives the client rectangle.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: Specifies the dots per inch (dpi) for the window.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was successful in getting the client rectangle.

function.name: get_client_rect
function.description: This function retrieves the coordinates of a window's client area. The client coordinates specify the upper-left and lower-right corners of the client area. Because client coordinates are relative to the upper-left corner of a window's client area, the coordinates of the upper-left corner are (0,0).

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose client coordinates are to be retrieved.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that receives the client coordinates. The left and top members are zero. The right and bottom members contain the width and height of the window.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI for the window.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns whether the function was successful or not.

function.name: get_window_info
function.description: This function retrieves information about a specified window and stores it in a WINDOWINFO structure.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which information is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: Pointer to a WINDOWINFO structure to receive the information.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function succeeds, or FALSE otherwise.

function.name: get_window_region
function.description: This function retrieves the region of a window. It allocates memory for the region data, makes a server request to get the window region, and then creates the region using the received data. If the server call returns a buffer overflow status, the function repeats the process with a larger buffer size. The function also retrieves the visible rectangle of the window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the region is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: surface
parameters.description: Boolean value that specifies whether to retrieve the surface region of the window.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Pointer to a variable that receives the handle to the region of the window.

parameters.name: visible
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that receives the visible rectangle of the window.

function.return_type: NTSTATUS, represents the status of the function execution. If the function succeeds, the return value is STATUS_SUCCESS. If the function fails due to insufficient memory, the return value is STATUS_NO_MEMORY. If the function fails due to a buffer overflow, the function repeats the process with a larger buffer size and the return value is STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW.

function.name: update_surface_region
function.description: This function updates the region of a surface associated with a window. It first gets the window pointer and checks if it's valid and not a desktop or other process. If the window has a surface, it gets the window region and creates a region from the visible rectangle. It then combines the shape and region, mirrors the region if the window style is RTL, and sets the shape of the window surface. It then gets the window region again and sets the clip of the window surface to the region or shape, offsetting the region if necessary. Finally, it cleans up by deleting any created regions and releasing the window pointer.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window whose surface region is to be updated.

function.return_type: void, meaning it does not return any value

function.name: get_visible_rect
function.description: This function calculates and returns the visible rectangle of a window, taking into account the window's style, extended style, and whether it is shaped or not.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the visible rectangle is to be calculated.

parameters.name: shaped
parameters.description: Indicates whether the window is shaped or not.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: The style of the window.

parameters.name: ex_style
parameters.description: The extended style of the window.

parameters.name: rects
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure containing the window and client rectangles.

function.return_type: RECT. Represents the visible rectangle of the window.

function.name: get_surface_rect
function.description: This function adjusts the surface rectangle based on the visible rectangle and the virtual screen rectangle. It crops surfaces larger than the virtual screen rectangle and offsets the surface rectangle by the top left coordinates of the visible rectangle. It also rounds the surface coordinates to avoid frequent re-creation on resize.

parameters.name: visible_rect
parameters.description: Pointer to the visible rectangle structure.

parameters.name: surface_rect
parameters.description: Pointer to the surface rectangle structure. This structure is modified by the function.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the surface rectangle was successfully adjusted, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: get_default_window_surface
function.description: This function retrieves the default window surface for a given window. It checks if the window is valid and not a desktop or other process window. If the window has a previous surface that matches the provided surface rectangle, it reuses it. If the window is a top-level window, it assigns a dummy surface. For child windows, it uses the parent's surface.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the default surface is to be retrieved

parameters.name: surface_rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that specifies the surface rectangle

parameters.name: surface
parameters.description: Pointer to a pointer to a window_surface structure. This is where the function will store the retrieved surface

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully retrieves the window surface, and FALSE otherwise

function.name: get_window_surface
function.description: This function retrieves the window surface for a given window. It takes into account various properties of the window such as its parent, style, shape, visibility, and whether it is layered or not. It also handles the creation of a new surface if necessary.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the surface is being retrieved

parameters.name: swp_flags
parameters.description: Flags that control the size and position of the window

parameters.name: create_layered
parameters.description: Flag indicating whether to create a layered window

parameters.name: rects
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure containing the window's rectangle information

parameters.name: surface_rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure to receive the surface rectangle

function.return_type: struct window_surface * - Pointer to the window surface structure. Returns NULL if the surface could not be retrieved or created

function.name: update_children_window_state
function.description: This function updates the state of all child windows of a given window. It first lists all child windows, then checks if each has a client surface, and if so, updates the window state. Finally, it frees the memory allocated for the list of child windows.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the parent window whose child windows' states are to be updated.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return any value.

function.name: get_icon_info
function.description: This function retrieves information about an icon or a cursor.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: Handle to the icon to get information about

parameters.name: ii
parameters.description: Pointer to an ICONINFO structure that receives the information about the icon

function.return_type: HICON, represents the handle to the icon if the function is successful, otherwise NULL

function.name: get_window_icon_info
function.description: This function retrieves the icon information for a given window. It tries to get the icon info in several ways and returns the first successful result. If no icon info can be obtained, it returns NULL.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the icon information is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The type of icon to be retrieved.

parameters.name: icon
parameters.description: Handle to the icon.

parameters.name: ret
parameters.description: Pointer to an ICONINFO structure that receives the icon information.

function.return_type: HICON. It represents the handle to the icon if the icon information is successfully retrieved, otherwise NULL.

function.name: apply_window_pos
function.description: This function applies the position and size of a window, and updates its surface and other related properties.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window.

parameters.name: insert_after
parameters.description: Handle to the window to insert after.

parameters.name: swp_flags
parameters.description: Flags that specify the size and position of the window.

parameters.name: new_surface
parameters.description: Pointer to the new surface of the window.

parameters.name: new_rects
parameters.description: Pointer to the new rectangle of the window.

parameters.name: valid_rects
parameters.description: Pointer to the valid rectangle of the window.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully applies the window position, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: expose_window_surface
function.description: This function exposes a window surface, handles its reference count, redraws the window if necessary, locks and unlocks the surface, and releases the surface when done.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to control the behavior of the function.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that specifies the area to be exposed.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI value for the window.

function.return_type: BOOL, where TRUE indicates that the function succeeded and FALSE indicates that it failed.

function.name: NtUserGetWindowRgnEx
function.description: This function retrieves the window region of a specified window, combines it with a specified region, and deletes the window region.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose window region is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: hrgn
parameters.description: Handle to the region to be combined with the window region.

parameters.name: unk
parameters.description: An unknown parameter.

function.return_type: int, represents the status of the function execution. Returns ERROR if the window region retrieval fails, otherwise returns the status of the region combination operation.

function.name: NtUserSetWindowRgn
function.description: This function sets the window region of a given window. If a region is provided, it is used, otherwise the existing region is cleared. The function also handles redrawing and DPI scaling.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose region is to be set.

parameters.name: hrgn
parameters.description: Handle to the region to be set. If this parameter is NULL, the existing window region is cleared.

parameters.name: redraw
parameters.description: Specifies whether the system redraws the window after setting the window region. If this parameter is TRUE, the system does so; otherwise, it does not.

function.return_type: int, represents whether the function was successful or not. Returns TRUE if successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: NtUserMoveWindow
function.description: This function moves a window to a new location and optionally resizes it.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window to move.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The new position of the left side of the window.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: The new position of the top of the window.

parameters.name: cx
parameters.description: The new width of the window.

parameters.name: cy
parameters.description: The new height of the window.

parameters.name: repaint
parameters.description: Whether the window should be repainted following the move.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the window was successfully moved and resized.

function.name: NtUserGetLayeredWindowAttributes
function.description: This function retrieves the color key, alpha value, and flags for a layered window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the layered window

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable that receives the color key of the layered window

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable that receives the alpha value of the layered window

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable that receives the layered window attributes

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function successfully retrieved the window attributes or not

function.name: NtUserSetLayeredWindowAttributes
function.description: This function sets the attributes for a layered window. It first sends a request to the server to set the window layered info. If the request is successful, it sets the layered window attributes and updates the window state.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Specifies the color key

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.description: Specifies the alpha value

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Specifies the flags

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was successful in setting the layered window attributes and updating the window state

function.name: NtUserUpdateLayeredWindow
function.description: This function updates the attributes of a layered window with the specified parameters.

parameters.description: Pointer to the blend function for the layered window

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Specifies the flags for the layered window

parameters.name: dirty

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function succeeds, or FALSE otherwise

function.name: list_children_from_point
function.description: This function retrieves a list of child windows from a given point. It dynamically allocates memory for the list, and if the memory allocation fails or no child windows are found, it returns NULL.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the parent window.

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: Structure that specifies the x- and y-coordinates of the point.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI setting for the window.

function.return_type: HWND*. It returns a pointer to the list of child window handles. If no child windows are found or memory allocation fails, it returns NULL.

function.name: window_from_point
function.description: This function retrieves a handle to the window that contains the specified point and determines the hit-test value. It can also send a WM_NCHITTEST message to the window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window. If this parameter is NULL, the function uses the desktop window.

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: A POINT structure that specifies the point to be checked.

parameters.name: hittest
parameters.description: Pointer to an integer that receives the hit-test value. It can be one of the HT* values.

parameters.name: send_nchittest
parameters.description: Specifies whether to send a WM_NCHITTEST message to the window that contains the point. If this parameter is TRUE and the thread that owns the window is not hung, the function sends a WM_NCHITTEST message.

function.return_type: HWND. If the function succeeds, the return value is a handle to the window that contains the point. If no window exists at the given point, the return value is NULL. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.

function.name: NtUserWindowFromPoint
function.description: This function returns the window that contains the specified point.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the point.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: The y-coordinate of the point.

function.return_type: HWND, represents a handle to the window that contains the point.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Handle to the parent window.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the point.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: The y-coordinate of the point.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: The child window must meet these criteria.

function.return_type: HWND, represents a handle to the child window that contains the point and meets the criteria specified by uFlags. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.

function.name: NtUserRealChildWindowFromPoint
function.description: This function returns the child window of a parent window that lies at the specified point.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Handle to the parent window.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the point.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: The y-coordinate of the point.

function.return_type: HWND, represents the handle to the child window at the specified point.

function.name: get_maximized_rect
function.description: This function gets the maximized rectangle of a window. It first retrieves the monitor information for the window, then checks the window's style. If the window has a maximize box, a caption, and is not a child window, it adjusts the rectangle to the work area of the monitor.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which to get the maximized rectangle.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that receives the maximized rectangle.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE always indicating the function executed successfully.

function.name: update_maximized_pos
function.description: This function updates the maximized position of a window. If the window is maximized and not minimized, it gets the monitor information and updates the window's maximized position based on the work area of the monitor. If the window is not maximized, it sets the maximized position to -1.

parameters.name: wnd
parameters.description: This parameter is a pointer to the window structure whose maximized position is to be updated.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return any value.

function.name: empty_point
function.description: This function checks if the given point is at the position (-1, -1).

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: The point to check.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the point is at the position (-1, -1), otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: NtUserGetWindowPlacement
function.description: This function retrieves the show state and the restored, minimized, and maximized positions of the specified window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window.

parameters.name: placement
parameters.description: A pointer to the WINDOWPLACEMENT structure that receives the show state and position information.

function.return_type: BOOL, where TRUE indicates success and FALSE indicates failure.

function.name: make_rect_onscreen
function.description: This function adjusts the position of a rectangle to ensure it is within the screen boundaries. It uses the monitor information corresponding to the rectangle and the thread's DPI.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the rectangle that needs to be adjusted to fit within the screen boundaries.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return anything but modifies the rectangle passed to it in-place.

function.name: NtUserGetInternalWindowPos
function.description: This function retrieves the show state and the restored, minimized, and maximized positions of the specified window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: A pointer to a RECT structure that receives the restored window position.

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: A pointer to a POINT structure that receives the restored window position.

function.return_type: UINT, represents the current show state of the window. It returns zero if the function fails.

function.name: make_point_onscreen

It first creates a rectangle with the point as the top left corner and a size of 1x1, then adjusts the rectangle to be onscreen, and finally sets the point's coordinates to the top left corner of the adjusted rectangle.

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: A pointer to the point to be adjusted.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return a value but modifies the point in place.

function.name: set_window_placement
function.description: This function adjusts the placement of a window based on the provided parameters. It checks the flags to determine which placements to adjust (minimum, maximum, or normal). It also handles different window styles (minimized, maximized, or normal).

parameters.description: Handle to the window whose placement is to be set.

parameters.name: wndpl
parameters.description: Pointer to a WINDOWPLACEMENT structure that contains the new window placement information.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags indicating which placements to adjust.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window placement was successfully set, and FALSE otherwise.

function.name: NtUserSetWindowPlacement
function.description: This function sets the placement of a window based on the WINDOWPLACEMENT structure provided. It also sets flags based on the WINDOWPLACEMENT structure and returns the result of the set_window_placement function.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose placement is to be set.

parameters.name: wpl
parameters.description: Pointer to a WINDOWPLACEMENT structure that contains the new window placement information.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the window placement was successfully set or not.

function.name: NtUserBuildHwndList

parameters.name: buffer

parameters.name: size

function.name: NtUserFindWindowEx

parameters.name: parent

parameters.name: child

parameters.name: class

parameters.name: title

function.name: get_server_window_text
function.description: This function retrieves the text of a window from the server.

function.return_type: data_size_t, represents the length of the text retrieved from the server.

function.name: client_to_screen

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window whose client area is used for the conversion.

parameters.name: pt

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully converts the coordinates, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: screen_to_client
function.description: This function converts screen coordinates to client coordinates for a specified window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose client area will be used for the conversion.

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: Pointer to a POINT structure that contains the screen coordinates to be converted.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the conversion is successful, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: map_window_region
function.description: This function maps a region from one window to another, taking into account the offset and mirroring. If the windows are mirrored, it adjusts the region's coordinates accordingly.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Handle to the source window from which the region is to be mapped.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Handle to the destination window to which the region is to be mapped.

parameters.name: hrgn
parameters.description: Handle to the region to be mapped.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return a value but performs actions based on the provided parameters.

function.name: map_window_points
function.description: This function maps the points of one window to another. It adjusts the points based on the offset between the two windows and flips the x-coordinates if the windows are mirrored. In a special case when the count is 2, it swaps the x-coordinates of the two points.

parameters.name: hwnd_from

parameters.name: hwnd_to
parameters.description: Handle to the window to which points are to be mapped.

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Pointer to an array of POINT structures that contain the set of points to be mapped.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of POINT structures in the array.

parameters.name: dpi
parameters.description: The DPI setting for the window.

function.return_type: int, represents the low-order word of the new x-coordinate and the high-order word of the new y-coordinate if the function succeeds. Otherwise, it returns zero.

function.name: dump_winpos_flags
function.description: This function checks the status of various window position flags and logs them if they are set.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: This parameter represents the window position flags to be checked.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return any value

function.name: map_dpi_winpos
function.description: This function maps the DPI (dots per inch) of a window position, adjusting the coordinates and size according to the DPI settings.

parameters.name: winpos
parameters.description: A pointer to a WINDOWPOS structure that contains the size and position of a window.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value. It modifies the WINDOWPOS structure passed to it.

function.name: calc_winpos
function.description: This function calculates the new position and size of a window. It sends a WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING message, gets the window pointer, calculates new position and size based on various conditions, and finally releases the window pointer.

parameters.name: winpos

parameters.name: old_rects
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure that contains the old window rectangles

parameters.name: new_rects

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully calculates the new position and size, otherwise returns FALSE

function.name: get_valid_rects

parameters.name: old_client

parameters.name: new_client
parameters.description: Pointer to the new client rectangle

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags to determine the behavior of the function

parameters.name: valid
parameters.description: Pointer to the valid rectangles to be set by the function

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value but modifies the valid rectangles based on the input parameters

function.name: calc_ncsize
function.description: This function calculates the new client area of a window and returns the flags that determine the redrawing options.

parameters.name: winpos
parameters.description: Pointer to a WINDOWPOS structure that contains information about the window's position.

parameters.name: old_rects
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure that contains the old window and client rectangles.

parameters.name: new_rects
parameters.description: Pointer to a structure that contains the new window and client rectangles.

parameters.name: valid_rects
parameters.description: Pointer to an array of rectangles that will receive the valid update areas.

parameters.name: parent_x
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the parent window's client area.

parameters.name: parent_y
parameters.description: The y-coordinate of the parent window's client area.

function.return_type: UINT, represents the flags that determine the redrawing options for the window.

function.name: fixup_swp_flags
function.description: This function validates and adjusts the window position and size flags. It also checks the window's visibility and position in the z-order, and sets the appropriate flags.

parameters.name: winpos
parameters.description: Pointer to a WINDOWPOS structure that contains information about the window's position and size.

parameters.name: old_window_rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that contains the old window rectangle.

parameters.name: parent_x
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the parent window.

parameters.name: parent_y
parameters.description: The y-coordinate of the parent window.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully adjusts the flags, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: swp_owner_popups
function.description: This function adjusts the z-order of windows to ensure that popups stay above their owner windows. It also handles various window positioning scenarios based on the 'after' parameter.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window that needs to be adjusted.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Handle to the window after which 'hwnd' should be placed in the z-order.

function.return_type: HWND, represents the handle to the window after which 'hwnd' is placed in the z-order.

function.name: set_window_pos
function.description: This function sets the position of a window. It checks the z-order arguments, ensures the coordinates are valid for WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGING, performs common operations, handles the visibility of the window, handles the activation of the window, erases parent when hiding or resizing child, and sends the WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGED message.

parameters.name: winpos
parameters.description: Pointer to a WINDOWPOS structure that contains information about the window's size and position

parameters.name: parent_x
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the parent window

parameters.name: parent_y
parameters.description: The y-coordinate of the parent window

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the function was successful in setting the window position or not

function.name: NtUserSetWindowPos
function.description: This function sets the position and dimensions of a window. It also sets the Z order of the window and updates the window flags.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Handle to the window to insert after in Z order

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: New position of the left side of the window

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: New position of the top of the window

parameters.name: cx
parameters.description: New width of the window

parameters.description: New height of the window
