function.name: NtUserBeginDeferWindowPos
function.description: This function begins the process of changing the size and position of multiple windows in a single operation. It allocates memory for the operation and returns a handle to the memory.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of windows for which the size and position should be changed. If the count is zero, the function allocates memory for 8 moves. If the count is less than zero, the function sets the last error to ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER and returns 0.

function.return_type: HDWP. This is a handle to the memory allocated for the operation. If the function fails to allocate memory, it returns 0.

function.name: NtUserDeferWindowPosAndBand
function.description: This function defers the position and band of a window. It checks if the window is valid, adjusts the window position according to the DPI settings, and merges the changes with existing ones or adds a new position if necessary.

parameters.name: hdwp
parameters.description: Handle to a multiple-window – position structure that contains size and position information for one or more windows.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Handle to the window to insert after.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Specifies the new position of the left side of the window.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Specifies the new position of the top of the window.

parameters.name: cx
parameters.description: Specifies the new width of the window.

parameters.name: cy
parameters.description: Specifies the new height of the window.

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Specifies the window sizing and positioning flags.

parameters.name: unk1
parameters.description: Unknown parameter.

parameters.name: unk2
parameters.description: Unknown parameter.

function.return_type: HDWP, represents the updated multiple-window – position structure.

function.name: NtUserEndDeferWindowPosEx
function.description: This function ends the window positioning process that was started by a previous call to the BeginDeferWindowPos function. It also sends the WM_WINE_SETWINDOWPOS message to the window procedure of each window affected by the positioning operation.

parameters.name: hdwp
parameters.description: Handle to a multiple-window - position structure that contains size and position information for one or more windows.

parameters.name: async
parameters.description: Boolean value that indicates whether the function should be asynchronous or not. Currently, asynchronous operation is not supported.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function succeeds, or FALSE otherwise.

function.name: NtUserSetInternalWindowPos
function.description: This function sets the internal position of a window. It modifies the WINDOWPLACEMENT structure and calls the set_window_placement function to apply the changes.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose position is to be set.

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: Command to show the window.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that specifies the new coordinates of the window.

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: Pointer to a POINT structure that specifies the new minimum position of the window.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value

function.name: win_set_flags
function.description: This function sets and clears specific flags for a window, and returns the original flags.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose flags are to be set and cleared.

parameters.name: set_mask
parameters.description: Flags to be set for the window.

parameters.name: clear_mask
parameters.description: Flags to be cleared for the window.

function.return_type: UINT, represents the original flags of the window before setting and clearing.

function.name: can_activate_window
function.description: This function checks if a window can be activated based on its style properties.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This parameter is a handle to the window to be checked.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window can be activated, FALSE otherwise.

function.name: activate_other_window
function.description: This function activates another window based on certain conditions. It first checks if the given window is a popup and has an owner, if so it tries to activate the root ancestor of the owner. If it can't, it then tries to activate the next window in the Z order. If it still can't, it tries to activate the first child of the desktop window. If all these fail, it sets the foreground window to the given window if it's not already the foreground window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window that needs to be activated

function.return_type: void, meaning it does not return any value

function.name: send_parent_notify
function.description: This function checks if a window is a child window and not set to ignore parent notifications. If these conditions are met, it retrieves the parent of the window and sends a notification message to it.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window.

parameters.name: msg
parameters.description: The message to be sent to the parent window.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value.

function.name: get_min_max_info
function.description: This function retrieves the minimum and maximum window dimensions and positions for a given window handle.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window for which the minimum and maximum information is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: MINMAXINFO, a structure that contains the information about the minimum and maximum window dimensions and positions.

function.name: get_first_minimized_child_pos
function.description: This function calculates the position of the first minimized child window based on the parent window's dimensions and the minimized metrics.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the parent window's rectangle structure which contains the dimensions of the parent window.

parameters.name: mm
parameters.description: This is a pointer to the minimized metrics structure which contains information about the arrangement and spacing of minimized windows.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: This is the width of the child window.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: This is the height of the child window.

function.return_type: POINT, which represents the calculated position of the first minimized child window.

function.name: get_next_minimized_child_pos
function.description: This function calculates the next position for a minimized child window based on the current position, window size, and arrangement settings.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that specifies the parent window.

parameters.name: mm
parameters.description: Pointer to a MINIMIZEDMETRICS structure that contains the arrangement settings.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The width of the child window.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The height of the child window.

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Pointer to a POINT structure that specifies the current position of the child window. The function updates this structure with the next position.

function.return_type: void, as this function does not return a value but modifies the pos parameter to reflect the next position.

function.name: get_minimized_pos
function.description: This function calculates the minimized position of a window. If the window is already in a suitable position, it returns the current position. Otherwise, it finds the first available minimized position that is not occupied by another icon.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window whose minimized position is to be calculated.

parameters.name: pt
parameters.description: Current position of the window.

function.return_type: POINT, representing the minimized position of the window.

function.name: window_min_maximize
function.description: This function handles the minimizing, maximizing, and restoring of a window. It adjusts the window's size and position based on the command received and the window's current state.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window to be minimized, maximized, or restored.

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: Command to determine the action to be taken on the window. It could be minimize, maximize, restore, etc.

parameters.name: rect
parameters.description: Pointer to a RECT structure that receives the new dimensions and position of the window.

function.return_type: UINT. It represents the flags that indicate how the window is to be shown. It could be SWP_NOSIZE, SWP_NOMOVE, SWP_NOCOPYBITS, SWP_STATECHANGED, etc.

function.name: NtUserArrangeIconicWindows
function.description: This function arranges all the iconic (minimized) child windows of a parent window.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Handle to the parent window whose iconic child windows are to be arranged.

function.return_type: UINT, represents the number of iconic child windows arranged.

function.name: update_window_state
function.description: This function updates the state of a window. It sets the thread DPI awareness context, gets the window rectangles, gets the window surface, applies the window position, and finally resets the thread DPI awareness context.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window whose state is to be updated.

function.return_type: void, meaning it does not return a value

function.name: show_window
function.description: This function is used to show or hide a window, minimize or maximize it, or restore it to its original size and position. It also handles the visibility of the window and its parent, and sends appropriate messages for window events.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window.

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: The command to be executed. This can be a command to show or hide the window, minimize or maximize it, or restore it to its original size and position.

function.return_type: BOOL. It returns TRUE if the window was visible before the function was called, otherwise it returns FALSE.

function.name: NtUserShowWindowAsync
function.description: This function is used to show or hide a window asynchronously. It first checks if the window is a broadcast window, if so, it sets the last Win32 error to ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER and returns FALSE. If the window is the current thread window, it shows the window with the specified command. Otherwise, it sends a message to the window to show it.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window to be shown or hidden

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: Command to be executed, typically to show or hide the window

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the operation was successful or not

function.name: NtUserShowWindow
function.description: This function is used to show or hide a window based on the command provided. It also checks if the window is already visible or hidden before performing the action.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window to be shown or hidden

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: Command to either show or hide the window

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the operation is successful, FALSE otherwise

function.name: NtUserShowOwnedPopups
function.description: This function shows or hides pop-up windows owned by the specified window based on the 'show' parameter. It iterates through all the windows, checks if the window is owned by the specified owner and then sends a message to show or hide the window based on the 'show' parameter and the current state of the window.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Handle to the window that owns the pop-up windows.

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: Boolean value that specifies whether to show or hide the pop-up windows. If this parameter is TRUE, the pop-up windows are shown; if it is FALSE, the pop-up windows are hidden.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function executes successfully, regardless of whether the windows were shown or hidden.

function.name: NtUserFlashWindowEx
function.description: This function is used to flash the specified window. It changes the state of the specified window's title bar as specified by the FLASHWINFO structure. If the window is minimized and the system has a taskbar, the window's taskbar button will flash. Once flashing has started, it will be stopped by the system after a specified number of times or the system will stop flashing when the window comes to the foreground.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: This is a pointer to a FLASHWINFO structure that specifies the type of flashing to be done.

function.return_type: BOOL. The function returns TRUE if the function succeeds, FALSE otherwise. If the window is not found or the function fails for other reasons, the return value is FALSE and the last error code can be retrieved using GetLastError.

function.name: NtUserGetWindowContextHelpId
function.description: This function retrieves the help context identifier, if any, associated with the window represented by the given handle.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window whose help context identifier is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: DWORD, represents the help context identifier associated with the window. If the window does not have a help context identifier, or if the function fails, the return value is zero.

function.name: NtUserSetWindowContextHelpId
function.description: This function sets the help context identifier for the specified window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: A handle to the window for which the help context identifier is to be set.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The help context identifier to be set.

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the function successfully sets the help context identifier, otherwise returns FALSE.

function.name: NtUserInternalGetWindowIcon
function.description: This function retrieves the icon associated with a window. It handles different types of icons and errors related to invalid window handles or parameters.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the icon is to be retrieved.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of the icon to be retrieved. It can be ICON_BIG, ICON_SMALL, or ICON_SMALL2.

function.return_type: HICON, represents the handle to the icon. If the function fails, it returns 0.

function.name: send_destroy_message
function.description: This function sends a destroy message to a window and its children. If the window is the owner of the caret, the clipboard, or is active, it performs specific actions. It also checks if the window still exists after the destroy message, as the message can trigger re-entrant calls to DestroyWindow.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window to be destroyed

parameters.name: winevent
parameters.description: Boolean value that indicates whether to notify the event of object destruction

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything

function.name: free_window_handle
function.description: This function is used to free the memory allocated to a window handle. It first checks if the window handle exists and is not owned by another process. If these conditions are met, it destroys the window on the server, sets the user handle pointer to NULL, unlocks the user, and frees the memory allocated to the window's scroll, text, and the window itself.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is the handle to the window that needs to be freed.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: destroy_window
function.description: This function is responsible for destroying a window and freeing all the resources associated with it. It handles the destruction of child windows, unlinking from the parent, sending the WM_NCDESTROY message, updating the window state if necessary, and freeing resources such as menus, cursors, surfaces, and drawables.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window to be destroyed

function.return_type: LRESULT, represents the result of the message processing and depends on the message sent. In this case, it always returns 0 indicating successful execution of the function

function.name: user_destroy_window
function.description: This function is used to destroy a window and perform necessary cleanup operations. It checks if the window belongs to the current thread and is not a desktop window, calls necessary hooks, ends the menu if active, checks if the window is a child window and sends a destroy notification to the parent if it is. If the window is not a child, it calls shell hooks. It then hides the window, destroys child windows if any, sends a destroy message and finally destroys the window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window to be destroyed

parameters.name: winevent
parameters.description: Boolean value indicating whether a winevent should be triggered

function.return_type: BOOL, returns TRUE if the window is successfully destroyed, FALSE otherwise

function.name: NtUserDestroyWindow
function.description: This function is used to destroy a window.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window to be destroyed.

function.return_type: BOOL, represents whether the window was successfully destroyed or not.

function.name: destroy_thread_windows
function.description: This function is used to destroy all the windows associated with the current thread. It recycles WND structs as destroy_entry structs, frees up resources associated with the windows, and then destroys the windows.

parameters.name: void
parameters.description: This function does not take any parameters.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return anything.

function.name: create_window_handle
function.description: This function creates a window handle with the specified parameters, and returns a pointer to the created window.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Handle to the parent window.

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Handle to the owner window.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Pointer to the name of the window.

parameters.name: class_instance
parameters.description: Instance of the window class.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: Instance of the window.

parameters.name: ansi
parameters.description: Boolean value indicating whether the window is ANSI or not.

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: Style of the window.

parameters.name: ex_style
parameters.description: Extended style of the window.

parameters.description: A pointer to a CREATESTRUCTW structure that contains information about a window's initial size and position.

parameters.name: dpi_to
parameters.description: The DPI value to which the DPI of the CREATESTRUCTW structure should be mapped.

function.return_type: void, this function does not return a value but modifies the CREATESTRUCTW structure passed as a parameter.

parameters.name: version

parameters.description: Pointer to the window name

parameters.name: style
parameters.description: Window style

parameters.name: cx

parameters.description: Height of the window

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Handle to the parent window

parameters.name: menu
parameters.description: Handle to the menu

parameters.name: class_instance
parameters.description: Handle to the instance of the class

parameters.name: params
parameters.description: Pointer to the parameters

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for window creation

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: Handle to the instance of the window

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: Pointer to the class

parameters.name: ansi
parameters.description: Boolean value indicating whether the window is ANSI or not

function.return_type: HWND, which represents the handle to the newly created window. If the function fails to create a window, it returns 0.

function.name: get_dialog_info
function.description: This function retrieves the dialog information associated with a given window handle. If the window handle is invalid or corresponds to another process or the desktop, it sets the last error to ERROR_INVALID_WINDOW_HANDLE and returns NULL.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: This is a handle to the window for which dialog information is to be retrieved.

function.return_type: void*: Returns a pointer to the dialog information of the window. If the window handle is invalid or corresponds to another process or the desktop, it returns NULL.

function.description: This function sets the dialog information for a given window. It first retrieves the window pointer, checks if it's valid and not pointing to another process or the desktop, then sets the dialog information and releases the window pointer.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window for which the dialog information is to be set.

function.name: NtUserDragDetect
function.description: This function detects if the user has dragged the mouse within a certain rectangle. It first checks if the left mouse button is down. If not, it returns false. If it is, it sets a capture on the mouse input and enters a loop where it checks for mouse messages. If the left button is released, it releases the capture and returns false. If the mouse moves outside the rectangle, it releases the capture and returns true.

parameters.name: hwnd
parameters.description: Handle to the window that receives the mouse input.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The x-coordinate of the point where the mouse was initially clicked.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: The y-coordinate of the point where the mouse was initially clicked.

function.return_type: BOOL. Returns TRUE if the user drags the mouse outside the rectangle, FALSE otherwise.
